question: With a common hidden program, identical context and executed history, can a support-fitted flat policy correctly change its next action when a newly observed cell contains one marker versus none?
population: Identical program rows and first at most six worlds as karel_trace_control_20261120.json. Independently interpret the published JSON AST and demand exact original primitive trace, successful termination and full recorded endpoint on EVERY included world, even those with no move. Stop on any mismatch or source/worker digest failure. Require exactly five other demonstration worlds for the paired policy test; report excluded counts for any other size.
pair: At the boundary just after the FIRST successful forward move in each native trajectory, share the entire expert primitive prefix including that move, original pre-action sensors, original initial world and the same five support demonstrations across both arms. Set the destination marker count to zero or exactly one. All other world and program state, pose, prefix, instruction pointer, and support data remain identical. At that instant the destination has not previously been visited. Worlds without a move are ineligible. Score the oracle's first next attempted primitive, even if it is illegal, or deliberate STOP. Keep such illegal requests in the primary denominator and report by arm. Guard a no-action infinite loop with 4096 control operations after injection; exclude both arms and disclose if either loops. Unknown syntax or failed native validation invalidates the run.
predictors: Freeze the existing live, initial-only and masked policies, same suffix length/tie-breaking/observation and masked fallback as karel_online_control_20261120.json. Fit on the other five unmodified demonstrations only. Feed teacher-forced original observations and actions up to the boundary; at that boundary the live policy sees the manipulated sensor bit. The other two have the same inputs in both arms. Never use reference program, alternative arm's action, target endpoint or later history for prediction. No fitting on these paired outcomes.
measures: Report incidence among all original worlds and all distinct program codes; report eligible/excluded/no-move/no-five-support/nonterminating-pairs and attempted illegal counts for oracle and policies by arm. Separate oracle-switch vs oracle-stay pairs. In each give distinct-program and world counts, correct zero arm, correct one arm, both-correct, per-arm and balanced accuracy, fraction predicting different actions, and program-macro versions by exact program code for each mode. Initial-only and masked predictions must coincide within each pair; upper bound balanced next-action accuracy of any deterministic paired-invariant predictor on switch pairs is 1/2, both-correct is 0. Stay pairs reveal unhelpful flips. Primary descriptive outcome is joint correct measured on the switch pairs and separately the stay pairs. No resampling, tuning, extra thresholds or claim of generalization.
decision: If fewer than 50 distinct validation program token-sequence SHA256s have an oracle switch, stop this probe for insufficient breadth, regardless of observed policy accuracy. If sufficient, report solved switches and stay errors and the arithmetic invariant bounds. No conclusion of hierarchical routing or novel latent feedback is possible from a flat policy.
limits: One teacher-forced local choice, synthetic marker-count intervention and partial local observations. The full known Karel state and program allow planning; changing the marker in a previously unvisited cell can be equivalent to choosing that cell's initial count. This is causal sensitivity to a newly available sensor value under a fixed information boundary. Not an on-policy rollout, original benchmark episode, physical deployment, or stochastic surprise.
